title: Compare Weave & Jellyfish: Real ROI for Engineering Teams
summary: Compare Weave and Jellyfish for AI ROI: explained code-output estimates, cost attribution, agent insights, pricing, and a practical evaluation workflow.
body_markdown:
The short version


Weave makes the output estimate explainable at the code-change level.


A routine fix and a complex refactor each produce a merged PR. Silk 1 estimates the expert effort represented by the code and explains its reasoning, with calibration from your team. Put that estimate beside AI costs, attribution coverage, quality and delivery. Jellyfish also links spend to work and outcomes; ask both vendors to demonstrate the measure behind the report.


### Weave


Weave combines Code Intelligence, Engineering Intelligence and Token Intelligence to investigate engineering output and AI investment. Silk 1 estimates expert effort from code changes. The platform connects that estimate with attribution, costs, delivery and quality; Wooly helps investigate underlying records. Expert hours are model estimates, not hours actually worked or saved.


### Jellyfish


Jellyfish spans AI impact, delivery, developer experience, investment allocation and finance. Its October 2026 release announced agent insights, spend-to-work attribution, cost reconciliation and AI Capacity. Its Oct. 7 recap marks the AI spend dashboard, Total R&D Cost and R&D cost per merged PR as available now; initiative-level AI spend allocation and AI capacity metrics are coming soon. Confirm rollout and availability for your account.

The key difference


## Inspect the work behind the ROI number


Weave


### Weave’s code-based estimate


Weave gives you an output definition to inspect: estimated expert effort for the code changes in a pull request. Read the explanation, compare routine and complex changes, and calibrate estimates with engineers who know the work. Then investigate costs and attribution against that defined output population.


1391011


Jellyfish


### Jellyfish’s documented approach


Jellyfish joins AI usage and spend with SDLC signals, initiatives and investment context. Its current materials describe throughput, cost forecasts, spend-to-work attribution and agent activity. The October launch also announced headcount-normalized AI Capacity, but its Oct. 7 recap says AI capacity metrics and initiative-level AI spend allocation are coming soon. The recap lists the spend dashboard, Total R&D Cost and R&D cost per merged PR as available now. Ask about availability, the denominator, allocation rules and underlying work records.


1391011


Choose Weave when an explained code-output estimate is central to the buying decision. It gives the budget discussion a code-level basis you can inspect. A documentation comparison does not establish that another vendor lacks a similar capability or that either method proves causal AI gains.


Two documented paths into an AI investment decision. Weave foregrounds its explained expert-effort estimate; Jellyfish foregrounds AI impact across the SDLC. Jellyfish's Oct. 7 recap lists its spend dashboard, Total R&D Cost and R&D cost per merged PR as available now; AI capacity metrics and initiative-level AI spend allocation are coming soon. Workflow schematic, not a performance ranking or a complete feature inventory.123891011

Choose for your workflow


## When Jellyfish may fit your team


Include Jellyfish when broad SDLC analysis, developer experience, investment allocation or DevFinOps drive the purchase. Its current AI product also covers agent behavior, costs and work attribution. If the decision depends on an explained effort estimate for code changes, start your Weave evaluation there and compare the actual outputs each vendor demonstrates.


810121


Try it on your own work


## Run a focused pilot before switching


1. 01


### Keep the reporting boundary consistent


Choose a representative repository, team and period. Record identity mapping, included work, excluded files, permissions and history. Preserve your existing baseline.


2. 02


### Inspect the measures behind the charts


Bring a routine fix, a refactor and an AI-assisted change your engineers understand. In Weave, inspect the effort estimate and explanation. In both products, ask how the report defines output, attribution, quality and missing data.


3. 03


### Reconcile the total cost


Match invoices, subscription allocations and connected-tool costs. Include platform modules and any separate Router plan. Review rework, acceptance and delivery before broadening the rollout; a lower cost ratio alone does not establish business ROI.
